dedupe_keys.name: geoboundaries global database of political administrative boundaries

description: geoBoundaries is an open database of political administrative boundaries for every country, with about one million boundaries in over 200 entities, including all UN member states, at up to five administrative levels. It is produced by the William & Mary geoLab with a community of contributors, which has tracked boundaries since 2016, to give researchers boundaries as each country would represent itself. Coverage is global; offerings are individual country files, global composite files with disputed areas marked, and simplified boundaries for cartography. Format and access: files are downloaded from the website or requested through an API in common GIS formats. Licence: CC BY 4.0 with required acknowledgement; free. Caveats: boundary vintages and sources differ between countries, the country files reflect national representations, not an arbitrated standard, and deeper levels are missing for many countries. For simulation it provides the reference units used to aggregate hazard exposure, resilience indicators and emergency response planning. Related catalogue records are WorldPop gridded population and AccessMod, which already use these boundaries as reference context.
